summary:
AGROLIFE is a simple, multilingual web app that works as a soil-quality radar for farmers. In Paraguay, 27% of the population farms for self-consumption and 53.6% works in family farming in rural areas. Many of these producers struggle to choose crops and plan rotations because of climate change, water scarcity and soil degradation. NASA data could help them, but it is spread across many platforms and hard to interpret.

AGROLIFE brings together NASA Earth observation data from SMAP Level-4 soil moisture (SPL4SMLM) and NASA Worldview. It turns that data into an interactive map that anyone can read. The app scores land quality from 1 to 100 based on soil moisture, temperature, porosity, drainage, texture and precipitation. It also shows daily rainfall and vegetation indicators (NDVI, EVI).

The challenge is to make NASA data useful for decisions on the ground. AGROLIFE meets it by translating complex measurements into clear ratings, such as “Excellent” or “Low”. This matters because better information helps family farmers protect their soil, save water, adapt to the climate and improve their yields and quality of life.
details:
AGROLIFE is a lightweight web dashboard built around a satellite map. When the app opens, it automatically loads data points for regions of Paraguay, such as Alto Paraná, Amambay and Caaguazú. It requires no login and no setup. Users can:

  • Zoom in and out, toggle information layers, draw field boundaries as polygons or import GeoJSON files.
  • Click the map to select an area and see its values below the map.
    • Physical: moisture, temperature, texture, porosity.
    • Weather: daily, weekly, monthly and accumulated rainfall, and monthly temperature.
    • Vegetation: NDVI, EVI, vegetation cover, overall vegetation status.
  • See a Land Quality score (1–100) with a breakdown by moisture, temperature, porosity, drainage, texture and precipitation, plus the date of the latest data.
  • Review a chart of events by category and a table of events and plots. Each row includes a direct link to its source in NASA Worldview.
  • Manage their own fields in “My parcels”. Each parcel records its name, location, area in hectares, crop type, coordinates, current parameters, measurement history and quality score.
  • Open a “Laws and regulations” panel. It links to Paraguay’s official bodies (MAG, SENAVE, MADES, INFONA) and key laws, such as Law 3742/09 on plant-protection products and Law 3239/07 on water resources.
  • Switch the language and choose between °C and °F.

Behind the interface, the app gets data from NASA SMAP (SPL4SMLM, version 8) and NASA Worldview. It turns raw values into simple ratings: Excellent / Very good / Good / Fair / Poor for moisture and fertility, and Very high to None for precipitation and porosity. API responses are cached for 10 minutes. If the connection fails, the user sees a clear error message instead of a technical error.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Turns hard-to-read satellite data into clear, practical information for small and family farmers.
  • Supports better decisions on what to plant, when to plant and how to rotate crops. These decisions take soil conditions and rain probability into account.
  • Encourages responsible use of water and soil, and helps farmers adapt to climate variability.
  • Saves farmers time and helps improve crop yields and quality of life in rural communities.
  • Connects agronomic data with the local legal framework, so farmers can also follow the rules on agrochemicals, water and land use.

Tools and technologies

  • Data: NASA SMAP L4 Soil Moisture (SPL4SMLM v8, NSIDC) and NASA Worldview (Earthdata). These provide soil moisture, temperature, precipitation, NDVI and EVI.
  • Software: a local web app with a data module that gets SMAP and Worldview data and returns it as DataFrames. The interactive map uses Leaflet with Esri satellite imagery, together with interactive charts and tables.
  • Design: a responsive, mobile-first interface (phones, tablets and computers) with a modern dark dashboard style.

Creativity
AGROLIFE does more than display NASA layers. It combines several datasets into a single 1–100 land-quality score that a farmer can understand at a glance. It brings together satellite data, personal field management and local regulations in one simple tool.

Factors the team considered

  • Simplicity: the app is built for non-technical users, so its scope is deliberately limited. It has no login, no database and no machine learning in this version.
  • Data accuracy: GeoJSON coordinates keep their [longitude, latitude] order so points fall in the right place. Every value links back to its NASA source.
  • Connectivity: caching and friendly error messages help in rural areas where internet access is limited.
  • Accessibility: the app supports several languages and units and is optimized for mobile phones, the device most farmers use.
  • Local context: the app covers Paraguayan regions and includes national agricultural and environmental regulations.
